notes: Both coders judged both documents as delegates; they aligned on 79 units and the final file has 98. Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly course-start vs before-course/general for syllabus-statement duties and during-work vs general for tool and data rules; resolved by what the sentence does (communicates expectations, governs use while working, or only defines). (2) modality: should vs must for first-person commitments and 'need to' duties (set to must), and informs vs must-not for sentences that classify conduct as misconduct (set to informs). (3) policy type: tier headings P05 vs P01/P02/P04 (P05 for all three headings, with the bans coded at the example statements), P49 vs P50 for the protected-data ban (P50), P81 vs P36 (P36, no procedure steps given), P14 vs P02 (P14), P52 vs P77 for vendor terms (P77), P25 vs P26 for the prompt/response appendix (P26). (4) actor: all vs student/admin, set to all when the sentence addresses the whole community. (5) unit_stance: disclosure duties under permitted use set to permit, not require. B split the appendix items and the penalty list more finely and found units A missed (pre-populated language, grade penalty for inaccurate output, legal-advice ban); A found units B missed (honor-and-integrity rationale, 'most assignments will permit AI', in-class instructor use). All one-coder units were real statements and were kept. One UNCOVERED unit (legal analysis or advice) kept; no new types.
